title: Label every input
summary: Give every form control a visible label.
paragraphs: A placeholder disappears as soon as someone types. Use a label that stays on the page and describes the value you expect.
Match the label htmlFor to the input id. This connects the name for assistive technology and makes the label clickable.
When validation fails, explain the correction in text next to the field. Do not depend on a red border alone.

title: Keep state small
summary: Store user choices and derive the rest.
paragraphs: A filtered list can usually be calculated from the original list and the current query. Keeping another copy in state introduces a second value to synchronize.
Calculate inexpensive derived values during rendering. Add memoization only after measuring a real cost.
Place state near the component that needs it. Moving everything to a shared provider makes simple interactions harder to trace.

title: Render text safely
summary: Treat user input as text rather than markup.
paragraphs: For a plain DOM page, assign user content with textContent. It displays characters without interpreting them as HTML.
React escapes ordinary string children. Keep notes as strings and render paragraphs instead of assembling markup from input.
When formatted HTML is a requirement, choose a reviewed sanitization approach. Escaping text and sanitizing HTML solve different problems.
